 Pitching in a game for the first time since July 4, Brandon Woodruff allowed one run in the ninth Monday to finish off Game 3 against the Rays.
 Woodruff, returning from a shoulder injury, allowed one run on a soft infield single and a ringing double from Yandy Díaz, but he looked fine in averaging 91.2 mph with his fastball and topping out at 93.1 mph. It was his first postseason appearance since the 2021 NLDS, when he lost a 3-0 game to the Braves and later pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings in relief.

 Brandon Woodruff has been added to the Brewers’ roster for the World Series, replacing Chad Patrick. 
 It’s the only change for Milwaukee. Woodruff just faced hitters for the first time Tuesday, throwing 23 pitches and reportedly averaging 90-92 mph with his fastball. He last pitched on July 4 before going down with a recurrence of a shoulder injury that was originally expected to require season-ending surgery. The choice to put him on the roster here carries some risk, as the Brewers probably won’t be allowed to replace him if he suffers a setback. He takes the spot of Patrick, who hadn’t pitched in the postseason despite turning in a 3.40 ERA in 106 innings this year.

 Brewers manager Pat Murphy said there still hasn’t been any decision on whether to include Brandon Woodruff on the World Series roster. 
 Woodruff, out since June after a shoulder setback, resumed facing hitters on Tuesday. The Brewers are concerned that Woodruff would likely be unable to be replaced on the World Series roster if he aggravates something while pitching. He’d probably be limited to one- or two-inning appearances if he does make the cut for the roster.

 Brandon Woodruff said he was sitting 90-92 mph while throwing 23 pitches to Brewers hitters Tuesday. 
 Woodruff is hoping to be included on the Brewers’ World Series roster after missing the last 4 1/2 months with a shoulder injury. His velocity apparently is back close to the 91.8 mph he averaged with his fastball in nine starts before going down this season. Still, it seems like something of a long shot that he’ll be activated.

 The Brewers might exclude Brandon Woodruff from the World Series roster out of concern that the league wouldn’t allow them to replace him in the event of a shoulder setback. 
 The rule for replacing injured players in the postseason is that it has to be a new injury, so the Brewers might be stuck with Woodruff on the roster and unable to pitch if something goes wrong. Woodruff hasn’t pitched since June because of a shoulder injury that was originally thought would require season-ending surgery. If he’s added to the World Series roster, it could be at the expense of Kyle Harrison, who has yet to pitch in the postseason.

 Brandon Woodruff (shoulder) confirmed the World Series would be the earliest he could return. 
 There hasn’t been any official clarity from either the Brewers or Woodruff after he underwent followup imaging on his shoulder in late September. The 33-year-old has been cleared to resume throwing and is presumably ramping up his pitch count and stamina in an effort to contribute if Milwaukee makes a deep postseason run.

 Brandon Woodruff (shoulder) is scheduled to undergo followup imaging later this week. 
 Woodruff is holding out hope that he’ll be able to pitch at some point during Milwaukee’s upcoming playoff run after managing to avoid season-ending shoulder surgery. He’ll undergo imaging to determine his next steps and whether he’ll be cleared to progress to throwing bullpen sessions.

 Brandon Woodruff (shoulder) is throwing from 105 feet. 
 As of now, the plan is for the Brewers to “re-evaluate him for mound readiness at the end of September.” While it’s great that Woodruff is building back up, the fact that he is not pitching off a mound and won’t even be evaluated until the end of the month makes it seem unlikely he will pitch meaningful innings this postseason. Perhaps if the Brewers are able to advance, he could give them some innings out of the bullpen or as an opener, but it remains to be seen how effective he will even be. 
 Brandon Woodruff 
 MIL 
 Starting Pitcher 
 #53 
 Brandon Woodruff (shoulder) has been cleared to start a throwing progression. 
 This qualifies as an all-time unexpected late-season development. Woodruff told reporters last month that he was undergoing season-ending capsule surgery on his right shoulder. That didn’t end up happening after followup imaging showed better than expected healing to the point that Dr. Keith Meister told him that surgery wasn’t required. He’ll begin a five-week throwing progression next week with the aim of being ready to pitch for Milwaukee in the postseason. Unreal. He won’t be ready in time to help fantasy managers down the home stretch, but his unexpected return would be a massive development for the Brewers heading into the playoffs. 
 Brandon Woodruff

 #53 
 Brandon Woodruff will undergo season-ending right shoulder capsule surgery. 
 The history of pitchers returning from multiple shoulder surgeries is extremely bleak, but Woodruff has insisted that he plans on pitching again. The 33-year-old former fantasy ace will miss the remainder of the current season in addition to a significant chunk of next year as well. He missed nearly a year and a half after undergoing a similar capsule repair procedure back in 2023. This latest development certainly helps explain why Milwaukee went out and acquire Lance McCullers Jr. from the Astros earlier this week.

 Facing elimination, the Rays will start Griffin Jax in Game 4 against the Brewers.
 Jax last started Game 3 against the Guardians in the ALCS and allowed three runs over four innings in what turned out to be a 3-2 loss for the Rays. It’ll be his first career World Series appearance.

 Jackson Chourio went 4-for-5 with an RBI double and a steal as the Brewers decimated the Rays 10-1 on Monday to open up a 3-0 lead in the World Series. 
 Chourio singled and scored in a two-run third and then had a two-hits as part of an eight-run fifth inning in which the Brewers collected seven straight hits with two outs. He has eight hits through three World Series games, and if things continue to play out like this, series MVP honors will probably come down to him or William Contreras. Game 4 is slated for Tuesday night. Both starters are TBA, though Griffin Jax and Dustin May figure to be involved.
 -  Matthew Pouliot

 Robert Gasser faced the minimum over six innings as the Brewers crushed the Rays in Game 3 on Monday.
 Gasser gave up a Yandy Díaz single to begin the bottom of the first, but he faced only three batters then after Chandler Simpson, who barely beat out a double play ball on which Díaz was retired, was caught stealing. The only other batter to reach was Victor Mesa Jr. on a walk in the sixth, and he was erased on a Nick Fortes double play. Gasser’s three postseason starts have seen him give up only one run in 15 innings. It’s a distant concern right now, but he’s probably locked up his spot in the 2027 rotation.

 Freddy Peralta was charged with five runs in 4 2/3 innings in losing Game 3 of the World Series against the Brewers.
 Peralta surrendered two runs in the third on three singles and a walk. The rest of the damage came in the fifth, which was very nearly a scoreless frame. However, an overturned call correctly got Christian Yelich second base ahead of Junior Caminero’s relay on a grounder to third with two outs. Peralta was then pulled with the bases loaded, and the Brewers went on to score eight runs, collecting four straight hits off Cam Booser and two more off Cole Sulser before the inning finally concluded. It was probably a very disappointing end to a stellar postseason run for Peralta, who was the ALCS MVP against the Guardians. But there’s still a chance the Rays will rally and give him one more chance.
 -  Matthew Pouliot

 Aranda has been a platoon player in the past, but not so much recently. He had started all of the Rays’ previous postseason games, and he’s hit .310/.383/.405 in 48 plate appearances.
